B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: SignNow says the hosted MCP server is included with existing paid plans with no separate tier or add-on. A free trial is also advertised; the documentation does not specify whether trial accounts can connect to hosted MCP.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Business at $8/user/month, Business Premium at $15/user/month, Enterprise at $30/user/month (annual billing); Site License at $1.50/signature invite. Monthly billing is higher. Pricing page advertises a 7-day free trial.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Pricing is subscription/per-user for named plans and per-signature-invite for Site License. Official pricing content states a limit of 100 invites per user/year for standard plans; the MCP-specific pages do not document separate fees or call quotas.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Hosted connection requires SignNow account authorization. User permissions are described as scoped to documents and templates. Docs advise reconnecting if access is revoked or a session expires. No MCP-specific admin switch, allowlist, or region restrictions were found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: SignNow account holder and vendor; organization permissions may also apply.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Hosted reference distinguishes read-oriented operations by function but provides no readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. Read tools include listing, retrieval, status, view, and download-link functions; write tools include creation, updates, invites, reminders, cancellation, and embedded-session/link creation. 2. send_invite is described as designed for confirmed sends; the AI typically previews and confirms recipients and sets preview_was_shown=True. This is documented as an AI workflow recommendation; server enforcement is not established. 3. Hosted OAuth metadata declares header bearer transport, scopes offline_access and *, authorization code and refresh token grants, DCR endpoint, and PKCE S256. Hosted docs describe account authorization scoped to documents and templates. Token duration, role inheritance specifics, admin switches, allowlists, and revocation details: Unknown. 4. Hosted docs specify one global endpoint and do not document read-only modes, toolsets, filters, query-free modes, or regional variants. 5. upload_document documents a safe base directory for local file paths (default user's home directory), supported file types, and a 40 MB maximum. No PII masking or field-level redaction is documented. 6. list_documents documents pagination default 50/max 100; list_all_templates default 50; list_contacts default 15/max 100. upload_document max 40 MB. Other quotas, rate limits, time-range caps, and per-call charges: Unknown. 7. Hosted docs describe parameter behavior for selected tools but no general unknown-argument rejection, coercion, or operator override rules. Several tools auto-detect entity type. 8. MCP request logging and audit behavior are not documented. Security docs claim no server-side data retention and runtime-memory processing. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or reporting action appears in the action inventory. No MCP upsell response is documented. 10. Repository README documents signnow_skills for listing/fetching bundled skill content; hosted tool reference does not list this tool. Docs recommend preview/confirmation before sending; whether hosted server enforces it is unknown. 11. Security docs describe no retained server-side state; cross-session memory behavior is not documented. 12. Official docs describe a single hosted endpoint. The repository also describes STDIO/local deployment and separate API Helper MCP documentation. 13. No raw API request, SQL, script, or arbitrary execution tool appears in the published tool names.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official hosted tool reference at https://docs.signnow.com/docs/mcp-tools names 20 tools and states no numeric total. The official repository README at https://github.com/signnow/sn-mcp-server lists 25 names, including five names absent from that hosted reference: send_invite_from_template, create_embedded_sending_from_template, create_embedded_editor_from_template, create_embedded_invite_from_template, and signnow_skills. These five are included as Official because their names appear in the vendor repository, but their deployed availability is unverified. Claude connector directory lists 16 tools; its subset omits four hosted-reference names and does not expose the five repository-only names. Tedix reports 16 tools, and MCP.so, apis.io, and Manufact provide differing or partial inventories; their counts do not replace official names.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tool reference says the assistant will typically preview and confirm recipients before sending, then pass preview_was_shown=True. The docs do not establish that the server independently enforces a human confirmation step. It also recommends resolving a recipient through list_contacts before sending.
F_documentation.governance_promises: MCP security docs state: “Your data is never used for AI training.” They also state: “The MCP server does not store your data server-side.” Other claims include scoped access to documents and templates, user-initiated actions, credential isolation, HTTPS transport, runtime-memory processing, and disconnect-based revocation. The general Privacy Notice describes broader personal-information processing, including AI model training for service purposes.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The overview says the server enables AI assistants to execute eSignature workflows. Security docs promise no MCP data use for AI training, no server-side data retention, and user ability to disconnect access.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The tool reference documents selected validation and size limits. The no-training, no-retention, scoped-access, and credential-isolation statements are documentation claims; the prepared code copy was incomplete, so server implementation was not independently verified. The preview and confirmation language is framed as typical assistant behavior, not proven server-side enforcement.

contradictions: Hosted official tool reference lists 20 tools; the official repository README lists 25, adding four template shortcut tools and signnow_skills. The repository is described as the server project and mentions the hosted endpoint, but whether these additional names are deployed at the input endpoint is unverified.
Claude connector directory lists 16 tools, fewer than the 20 in the hosted tool reference; its published subset omits list_contacts, create_template, upload_document, and view_document.

The MCP-specific security page says MCP-transmitted data is never used for AI training, while the general Privacy Notice says personal information may be used in AI model training for service purposes. The notices address different scopes; their relationship for MCP data is not clarified.
observations_for_research: The documentation places a preview and recipient confirmation in the expected assistant workflow and exposes preview_was_shown as an input; the available evidence does not show that confirmation is independently enforced by the server.
The same product has a global hosted endpoint and a local STDIO deployment. Hosted documentation, the official repository README, and connector directories publish different tool inventories.
Hosted OAuth scopes include the wildcard string "*" alongside offline_access; the docs do not explain the wildcard's permission semantics.
